name: Out-of-bounds Write
summary: The product writes data past the end, or before the beginning, of the intended buffer. On an ECU this can corrupt adjacent protocol state or execute attacker-controlled CAN payload bytes.
automotive: ISO/SAE 21434: treat as a cybersecurity weakness in the implementation of a communication item (CAN transport). Typical attack path is a malformed multi-frame TP.DT sequence.

name: Out-of-bounds Read
summary: The product reads data past the end, or before the beginning, of the intended buffer.
automotive: On CAN stacks, a short DLC or a sequence index that underflows can leak adjacent RAM.

name: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
summary: The product performs a calculation that can overflow or wrap, producing an unexpected index or length.
automotive: Classic in TP: sequence_number - 1 when sequence_number is 0 (uint8 wrap to 255).

name: Classic Buffer Overflow
summary: Copying a buffer without checking the size of input against the destination.
automotive: memcpy/strcpy of identification or DM16 payloads whose length comes from the bus.

name: Improper Input Validation
summary: The product receives input but does not validate or incorrectly validates that the input has the properties required.
automotive: TP.CM total size and package count must be checked against the stack maximum (e.g. 1785 bytes / 224 packages) before TP.DT writes.

name: NULL Pointer Dereference
summary: The product dereferences a pointer that is expected to be valid but is NULL.
automotive: Hardware callbacks left unset on a given platform.
